properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 23 at 5:00PM EDT until October 23 at 7:00PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Eastern Palm Beach County in southeastern Florida...

* WHEN...Until 700 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 458 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to nearly
stationary thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 3 inches of
rain have fallen during the last hour from the nearly stationary
thunderstorms.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are expected over
the area during the next couple of hours from the nearly
stationary thunderstorms. This additional rain will result in
minor flooding. If the rainfall amounts increase more than
forecast, then a Flash Flood warning may be needed for this area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
West Palm Beach, Boynton Beach, Lake Worth, Riviera Beach, Palm
Beach, Ocean Ridge, Greenacres, Palm Springs, Lantana, Atlantis,
Haverhill, Cloud Lake, President Donald J. Trump International
Airport, Gun Club Estates, Royal Palm Estates, Downtown West Palm
Beach, Schall Circle, Port Of Palm Beach and Lake Clarke Shores.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

* WHEN...In Effect.

* IMPACTS...A Small Craft Advisory means that wind speeds of 20

properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued October 23 at 12:45PM AKDT until October 26 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK

* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 8 to
16 inches. Winds could gust as high as 35 mph.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Saturday to 10 PM AKDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The snow will come in two waves. The first

inches of snow.

Mexico...

the flood of 1927.

late this evening. It will then fall below flood stage early
tomorrow afternoon.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 11.0
feet on 05/14/1941.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 23 at 4:31PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
At 431 PM EDT, National Weather Service meteorologists were tracking
strong thunderstorms along a line extending from 7 miles west of
Intersection Krome And U.S. 27 to near Fortymile Bend. Movement was
south at 10 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts of 45 to 50 mph and penny size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Fortymile Bend and Everglades National Park.
properties.instruction:
These winds can down small tree limbs and branches, and blow around
unsecured small objects. Seek shelter in a safe building until the
storm passes.

These storms may intensify, so be certain to monitor local radio
stations and available television stations for additional information
and possible warnings from the National Weather Service.

To report severe weather, contact your nearest law enforcement
agency. They will relay your report to the National Weather Service
office in Miami. You can also share your report with NWS Miami on
Facebook and Twitter.

properties.areaDesc: Mineral, CO; Rio Grande, CO; Saguache, CO
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 23 at 2:25PM MDT until October 23 at 5:00PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...The Flood Warning is cancelled for a portion of south
central Colorado, including the following areas, Mineral and Rio
Grande.

The heavy rain has ended. Please continue to heed remaining road
closures.

A Flood Watch remains in effect until 600 PM MDT Friday for a portion
of south central Colorado...

* WHERE...Southwestern Saguache, Central Mineral and Western Rio
Grande Counties...

* WHEN...Until 500 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Several structures are flooded and evacuations have
occurred from Wolf Creek Ranch to Fun Valley. Some roads remain
closed due to flooding including highway 160 and FR380. The Park
Creek bridge has been washed away with considerable debris in the
water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 223 PM MDT, Stream gauges indicate flooding continues for the
South Fork Rio Grande, Rio Grande between South Fork and Del
Norte, and other area streams.
- The South Fork Rio Grande and other area streams are past their
crests and are continuing to fall. The South Fork Rio Grande is
expected to fall back below Flood Stage late Friday night.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Del Norte, South Fork, Wagon Wheel Gap and Creede.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Move to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.
